pr_title: Wait for Home Assistant start in here_travel_time

## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->

Wait for Home Assistant to fully start before starting requests against the API.

The data coordinator depends on other entities e.g. `config.origin_entity_id` and `config.destination_entity_id` to specify the routing information. The integration must wait for those entities to be loaded before it can proceed to do the routing and fetching from the API

Alternative solution as described in #68744

Hi, thanks for working on this, hope you can fix the issue at hand.. 
please let me add this: seeing you now wait until HA to fully start, wont it cause other havoc? I already see this:
```
022-03-27 16:41:02 WARNING (MainThread) [homeassistant.components.homeassistant.triggers.numeric_state] Error initializing 'W bijna thuis' trigger: In 'numeric_state' condition: unknown entity sensor.here_w_naar_huis
2022-03-27 16:41:02 WARNING (MainThread) [homeassistant.components.homeassistant.triggers.numeric_state] Error initializing 'Marijn bijna thuis' trigger: In 'numeric_state' condition: unknown entity sensor.here_marijn_naar_huis
```

I fear that postponing the Here sensors to after the full startup, these automations will not be initialized in time either?

@Mariusthvdb thanks for providing up to date insights based on your advanced setup. I really appreciate it.

Based on your input we can deduct that this problem does arise for all travel time integrations.

I am not sure when automations are started. If they are only started after homeassistant is fully started it will be "better" but still a chance of a race condition exists.

EDIT: There cannot be a race condition. With the changes in this PR the `here_travel_time` entities get added right away (as apposed to never because of the error in the current `dev` state) but are `unknown` until Home assistant has fully started. As this can always happen e.g. when the API is not responsive or no internet the automations have to handle that in any case.
a yes, thats fine then, unknown is probably not an issue. thanks for your response. Guess these sensors are not restored? If that would be the case, these issues couldn't exist in the first place?
If you are still running the current dev version the sensors are not added/restored on startup -> They don't exist which explains your error messages.

sure, I understand that. I was talking about the new implementation of this PR. after creation, are they restored upon startup. Or do they behave like the template sensors, which need a full startup sequence to initialize.
Currently they do not get restored. But this should be a two line change in the future.

Two added lines don't get covered by unit tests. I tested them manually and the test coverage for this integration still is above 97%. I think trying to add test coverage for the two lines handling the case when homeassistant hasn't started yet is overkill. At least until someone can point me to a straightforward solution.

issue_context.body:
### The problem

see logs, config has been untouched, and as of todays nightly update no sensor travel time is computed.

seems something went wrong in https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/61398

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

2022.4.0.dev20220325

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

2022.4.0.dev20220324

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

Here travel time

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/here_travel_time/

### Diagnostics information

_No response_

### Example YAML snippet

```yaml
sensor:

# https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/here_travel_time/

  - platform: here_travel_time
    entity_namespace: here
    api_key: !secret rest_here_api_key
    name: Marijn naar huis
    origin_entity_id: device_tracker.marijn_app
    destination_entity_id: zone.home
    route_mode: fastest
    traffic_mode: true
    scan_interval: 2678400
```

It seems like we may still need some improvements to handle cases gracefully where the dependencies still fail to load.  That is, after dependencies sounds best effort.

Also, the sensor platform setup calls `await coordinator.async_config_entry_first_refresh()` which seems like it may block on this.  Does that need to be omitted ?

> It seems like we may still need some improvements to handle cases gracefully where the dependencies still fail to load. That is, after dependencies sounds best effort.

Yes this integration should fail gracefully if it couldn't find gps coordinates instead of calling the api and throwing errors.

> Also, the sensor platform setup calls await coordinator.async_config_entry_first_refresh() which seems like it may block on this. Does that need to be omitted ?

This was my initial idea, to remove that and overwrite `async_added_to_hass` like [google_travel_time](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/homeassistant/components/google_travel_time/sensor.py#L116).
But my tests showed that using `after_dependencies` does indeed already solve the error.

review_comments: We need to return None at the function body end explicitly. All exit points need to return a value explicitly if we return a value anywhere in a function.

Is it safe to call this immediately in `async_added_to_hass`?  The reason I mention this is because it felt a little difficult to follow the back and forth here since this calls a parent class of the method above, and it first read like a circular dependency.   I looked at the coordinator entity update and it seemed like it could work to call it since it handles coordinator update de-registration only.
I reread the coordinator code. I think it is the first time I fully understood it. Thanks for pointing that out!
